title: As a developer, I can run approximate nearest-neighbor similarity search over embeddings with configurable distance metrics
As a developer, I can combine dense vector search with keyword or sparse (BM25-style) signals in one hybrid query with fusion ranking
As a developer, I can run keyword/full-text search over documents inside the database without bolting on a separate search engine
As an ml-engineer, I can rerank search results with built-in or first-party-integrated reranking models
As a platform-engineer, I can see published benchmarks or measured latency/recall numbers backing the database's performance claims

As a developer, I can express rich filter conditions (ranges, geo, nested boolean logic, array membership) in queries
As a platform-engineer, I can isolate many tenants cheaply using namespaces, partitions, or per-tenant collections with documented limits
As a platform-engineer, I can scale beyond one node with sharding or distributed deployment
As a platform-engineer, I can replicate data across nodes or zones for high availability with a documented consistency model
As a platform-engineer, I can enforce granular access control (API keys, roles, per-collection permissions) on database operations

As a developer, I can use a fully managed cloud version of the database with programmatic provisioning
As a platform-engineer, I can deploy to production on Kubernetes with an official Helm chart or operator
As a developer, I can pay serverless usage-based pricing with transparent per-unit costs instead of provisioning fixed clusters
As a developer, I can prototype on a meaningful free tier before paying anything
As a developer, I can build against official SDKs in the major languages (Python, TypeScript, Go, Java)
As an ml-engineer, I can plug the database into RAG and agent frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, etc.) through maintained first-class integrations
